concept:
Districts are the divisions of a Holding that contain its Buildings.

Each Holding has a number of District slots, and this number grows with its Settlement Size. Every District is built with a primary Building and provides further slots for additional Buildings.

Beyond the Standard Districts, there are several specialized types:
•Holding Districts
•Resource Districts
•Duchy Districts
•Special Districts
•Great Districts
•Trade Post Districts
•Entrepôt Districts

districts.flavor: Officials of every rank work in the halls of this district, where the province's taxes are counted, its granaries are inspected, and its garrisons are paid.
districts.name: Governance Quarter

districts.flavor: A few coins from every batch struck in this district are locked away in a chest, to be tested later in case the minters grew greedy.
districts.name: Assay District

districts.flavor: The countryside pays for everything the duchy does, and in this district the bailiffs make sure of it, one field, herd, and village at a time.
districts.name: Bailiwick District

districts.flavor: The Theodosian Walls were built during the reign of Emperor Theodosius II in the early 5th century, but they still remain some of the most formidable fortifications built by human hands.
districts.name: The Theodosian Walls

districts.flavor: The Aurelian Walls were built during the reign of the Roman Emperors Aurelian and Probus. To this day they provide formidable defense, completely enclosing the seven hills of Rome.
districts.name: The Aurelian Walls

districts.flavor: Warehouses, scales, and counting rooms crowd the staple district, where the duchy's most valuable trade is weighed, taxed, and protected.
districts.name: Staple District

districts.flavor: Every gift to this endowment is given in perpetuity, and the clergy here hold charters from rulers whose names nobody else remembers.
districts.name: Endowment District

districts.flavor: Every soldier who musters in this district has their name, arms, and horse written into the roll. Those who fail to appear are written down too.
districts.name: Mustering Grounds District

districts.flavor: Guests in this district are hosted in halls and gardens fit for a duke, and more of the duchy's business is settled over dinner here than in court.
districts.name: Ducal Residence District

Allows reselling goods over long distances via its buildings

Imported goods are counted, sorted, and sent onward to market from these warehouses. The merchants here always know what is scarce, and charge accordingly.
districts.name: Entrepôt District

districts.flavor: This Great Project is not just a temple. It is a testament to our mettle. Our accomplishments. Our grandeur. A temple such as this signifies the rule and benevolence of our divine and powerful Devaraja.
districts.name: Capital Temple Complex

districts.flavor: This is the oldest part of the great wall, largely built by the Qin dynasty. The sands of time might have worn down stone, brick, and mortar, but it's still a formidable piece of fortification.
districts.name: The Great Wall

districts.flavor: A most impressive feat of engineering, this gargantuan wall has been expanded upon many times since its initial construction in the 7th century BC. It now stretches across thousands of miles and encompasses a large number of watchtowers, barracks, and garrison stations. Surely, no barbarian invader will ever overcome this mighty obstacle?

districts.flavor:
An early standing cathedral, seat of a bishop and a beacon for Christian pilgrims. Beneath heavy rounded arches and stately vaults, sacred relics and altars await the faithful.

Building Effects: … in Cathedral Complex
districts.name: Romanesque Grand Cathedral

districts.flavor: A place for republics to organize their government and manage their city.
districts.name: Great Plaza District

districts.flavor: A keep designed to not only house a reputable noble family, but also protect the surrounding town and farmlands.
districts.name: Castle Holding District

districts.flavor: A simple but effective tribal hold, standing guard over a tribal village.
districts.name: Tribal Holding District

districts.flavor: A populous city which houses a large number of burghers, merchants, and hard-working townsfolk.
districts.name: City Holding District

districts.flavor: A place of worship ruled by the clergy, surrounded by a town of faithful peasants.
districts.name: Temple Holding District

districts.flavor: A cluster of yurts breaks the monotony of the steppe. Everything here can be packed and moved to a new and more fertile location.
districts.name: Nomadic Settlement District

districts.flavor: A couple of small yurts clench anxiously, surrounded by a makeshift wall made out of dirt and animal feces that shields the herd from the harsh wind and serves as a fuel source for the fire.
districts.name: Herder Settlement District

districts.flavor: A place of equal parts worship and protection, massive walls surround these holy grounds.
districts.name: Temple Citadel Holding District

districts.flavor: This place of worship is not merely a great feat of engineering in itself, but is also a safe haven for pilgrims and the devout, and a testament to the piety of its commissioner. Though not considered a holy site, the magnificence of the building has caused the county to become a great religious hub in the region.
districts.name: Legendary Shrine

districts.flavor: A great and vast palace with surrounding gardens and hunting grounds. This luxurious abode not only provides comfort and entertainment to any ruler staying in it, but also functions as a status symbol of wealth and power.
districts.name: Legendary Palace

districts.flavor: The image of a legendary ruler now made immortal in stone. This monument not only celebrates the great deeds of its commissioner, but any who hold it within their domain claims custodianship of the legend itself.
districts.name: Legendary Statue

districts.flavor: This enormous towering monument is not merely daunting in its presence, but is also a highly defensible fortress in its own right and is used to defend the realm against would-be invaders.
districts.name: Legendary Watchtower

districts.flavor: This site has become famous for its strange and legendary wildlife, and so a vast hunting lodge has been built here to provide comfort to hunters seeking to make their names immortal.
districts.name: Legendary Hunting Lodge

districts.flavor:
Outside the city walls of Barcelona, at the feet of Montjuich hill, this great drydock arsenal arms and protects a fleet of war galleys.
Under pointed stone vaults workers labor tirelessly. Tall towers and long walls guard the secrets of their work from outsiders.
districts.name: Drassanes

districts.flavor:
This massive palace towers over the lush oasis of Merv. Fluted walls engulf workshops, armories and cavernous halls where emissaries and bureaucrats go about their business.
Half residence, half fortress, this great building is as capable of hosting the most magnificent of feasts as it is of repelling the most barbarous of raids.
districts.name: Great Kyz Kala

districts.flavor:
A gift of land and rights, in exchange for eternal salvation. That is the covenant which has been formed between the monastic community of Cluny and the local lord.
Over time, it has grown into a lively and influential community, free of secular interference, enforcing Benedictine discipline far and wide.

Under its many red roofs, monks pray, labor and illuminate manuscripts - a model for others to emulate throughout the continent.
districts.name: Cluny Monastery

districts.flavor: Running several miles long, these sprawling walls have protected the city since the time of the Caesars. The walls cleverly make use of the two rivers that snake through the meadowland, shielding it from enemies east and west. All traffic is channeled through specific chokepoints, the Bars, where toll can be extracted, or arrows and fire rained down.
districts.name: Walls of York

districts.flavor:
This mosque has a venerable story to tell. Here many centuries of spirituality and wondrous ingenuity are stratified one over the other as it is built on top of a Roman temple and an early Christian Basilica.
The building is renowned for its opulent and colorful marbles, as well as its golden mosaics pieced together by artists from as far as Constantinople.
districts.name: Great Mosque of Damascus

districts.flavor:
Legends say that the Jokhang was constructed over an ancient sacred lake, the heart of a demoness the shape of Tibet. Thrice it was raised, and thrice it was swallowed by the fury of the lake, before prayers and sacrificial offerings by the first emperor's wife were able to finally pacify it.
The temple is the most sacred in the land, a labyrinthine complex of courtyards and monastic residencies traversed by cavernous corridors and halls covered in yak butter.
districts.name: Jokhang Temple

districts.flavor:
In the Thuringian forest, perched atop a great, rocky precipice, this fortress controls all movement of goods and men through the region.
A heavy barbican guards the only access to the castle, and tall white walls snake through the crevices of the mountain. The Palas, is the most important building in the complex, a massive hall of cold stone warmed by the many hearths within.
districts.name: Wartburg

districts.flavor:
The Beta Giyorgis has been carved entirely out of a warm, red volcanic rock. Surrounding it are a dozen other sister temples and buildings, meant to represent both Earthly and Heavenly Jerusalem. This is living proof of the link between the Holy kingdom and this land.
Burrowed deep within the rock, the main hall of the church is lavishly painted with beautiful frescoes, while holy icons adorn the walls.
districts.name: St George of Lalibela

districts.flavor: This magnificent church has been modeled after the Hagia Sophia, to represent that same light, wealth and power in a frigid northern land. Austere, white limestone betrays the overwhelming colors of the frescoes within. Warmly lit by candles, shadows dance around the golden mosaics of the cathedral's many domes.
districts.name: Holy Wisdom of God

districts.flavor:
Massive walls of earth and mud, many feet high, surround the ancient city of Kano.
The earthworks cover far larger grounds than those inhabited by the townsmen, encircling wheat fields to sustain the population through long sieges.
districts.name: Kano Earthworks

districts.flavor:
For centuries Somapura has served as one of the most important learning centers in India, attracting scholars from far away regions thanks to its multitude of connections with Buddhist, Jain and Hindu monasteries.
The quadrangular plan represents the true harmony and purity of the universe, a perfect place for the mind to thrive.
districts.name: Somapura University

districts.flavor: The seat of the local archbishop and great source of civic pride for all the townsmen of Florence, the Duomo is one of the greatest feats of architecture ever conceived.
districts.name: Duomo of Florence

districts.flavor:
Worked on by thousands of artisans, the Konark Sun Temple is a massive temple dedicated to the sun god, Surya. The entire complex is built to resemble the mighty chariot of the god, carrying the light from the sea towards the east.
A marvelous example of Kalinga architecture the temple is covered in reliefs and sculptures, with gods, soldiers, musicians, and legendary creatures, narrating Hindu scriptures.
districts.name: Konarak Sun Temple

districts.flavor:
Founded by merchants and migrants from Kairouan, the sprawling complex has become one of the most prestigious centers of higher learning in the western Islamic world. It attracts scholars from far away regions and educates local elites in the finer subjects.
The madrasa is composed of several halls and rooms - offering a bed and rest to foreign students with Sahn as the central courtyard of public discussion.
districts.name: University of al-Qarawiyyin

districts.flavor:
Constructed to provide the city with fresh water in times of need, these massive reservoirs purify rainwater by acting as settling tanks and filtering down sediments.
The system is composed of several connected sections, from a smaller basin, to a larger one, to a decorated masonry water tank.
districts.name: Kairouan Basins

districts.flavor:
Surrounded by a sacred grove is the palace of the Ghanas - royal chieftains of the city.
The complex is made up of sandstone and mudbrick buildings and is protected by a gated enclosure. Its walls are covered in magnificently colored reliefs and carvings. A massive structure, this palace dominates the surrounding town.
districts.name: Ghana Palace

districts.flavor:
This citadel is a grandiose, impenetrable system of walls and towers. It protects the Danube bend and controls its rich trade. 
Visegrad citadel is composed of a lower portion with a powerful hexagonal tower facing the river, and an upper acropolis surmounting the tall hill. The massive triangular fortification works as a residence as well as an opulent hunting lodge.
districts.name: Visegrad Citadel

districts.flavor:
Constructed out of gneiss and limestone with the help of craftsmen from Germany, this great stone church is one of the first of its kind in the Polish lands and a testament to the power of the Church.
The massive walls offer the faithfull the promise of salvation and crucial mortal protection as well. The western tower is said to bear the marks of the Devil's talons, a testament to its defensive potential.
districts.name: Collegiate Church of St Mary and St Alexius

primaryBuilding.name: Collegiate Church of St Mary and St Alexius

districts.flavor:
Constructed by the early Chalukya dynasty these sacred caves have been cut deep into an imperious sandstone formation. Inside lies a most holy and silent inner world.
A triumphal gate leads pilgrims into the monolithic face of the mountain. The caves are decorated with idols from all the major faiths of India.
districts.name: Vatapi Caves

districts.flavor:
The golden walls of Jaisalmer houses not just a defensive installation but an entire city, in the middle of the Thar desert.
As the sun set the walls are said to turn a warm color of sweet honey, while at day they can make the city blend in with its surroundings.
districts.name: Golden Fort

districts.flavor: The guild halls here house the town's finest artisans, who guard their trade secrets jealously. Their work is excellent, their prices are high, and their apprentices are overworked.
districts.name: Guild District

districts.flavor: Local peasants, craftsmen, and merchants crowd this bustling square from dawn to dusk. Whatever the town cannot produce itself can be bought here, at a 'fair' price.
districts.name: Market District

districts.flavor: Piers and warehouses line the waterfront, where dockhands haul cargo from ships of every size. Whatever comes from across the sea, it comes through here first.
districts.name: Port District

districts.flavor: A chain of forts guards the edges of the barony, each manned by soldiers who know every road and ford. Raiders who come this way rarely get far.
districts.name: Border Forts District

districts.flavor: Sturdy stone walls surround the town, offering excellent protection from raiders. The townsfolk grumble about the toll at the gate, but it is still cheaper than being robbed.
districts.name: Walls District

districts.flavor: Sturdy barracks house the soldiers of the realm, keeping them fed, drilled, and ready to march. Keeping them sober is another matter entirely.
districts.name: Military District

districts.flavor: In these halls, officials of every rank copy, seal, and file the business of the realm. Their work is rarely praised, but without it the realm would soon grind to a halt.
districts.name: Bureaucratic District

districts.flavor: In these grand halls the ruler holds court. Behind high walls, the majesty of the realm is upheld by servants, skilled craftsmen and councillors alike. Some spend their entire lives without leaving this district.
districts.name: Royal Household

districts.flavor: Holy places crowd this quarter, their bells, chants, or calls to prayer marking every hour of the day. Here, the clergy hold nearly as much sway as the lord.
districts.name: Religious Enclave

requirements.name: Temple or Temple Citadel or Is a Theocratic-type Government

districts.flavor: The devout gather in this quiet community to live apart from the world, praying, farming, and copying holy texts. The world, however, keeps sending them its problems.
districts.name: Religious Community District

districts.flavor: Every temple, statue, and ceremony in this sacred quarter tells the same story: the king rules by the will of the gods. It is told often, and very loudly.
districts.name: Mandala District

requirements.name: Uses the Mandala Ornate Temple Great Project and Great District

districts.flavor: Marble, silk, and imported spices are ordinary sights in this quarter of wealthy households. The families here marry each other, lend to each other, and plot against each other.
districts.name: Patrician District

requirements.name: County capital or City

districts.flavor: Music, games, and spectacles of every kind draw townsfolk of all classes to this quarter. The nobles pretend not to enjoy it, and the peasants pretend not to notice them.
districts.name: Entertainment District

requirements.name: County capital or City

districts.flavor: Most of the city's people live in these crowded streets, several families to a roof. For newcomers from the countryside, it is the first step toward a better life.
districts.name: Housing District

requirements.name: County capital or City

districts.flavor: Across the countryside, manor houses are home to minor noble families who oversee the surrounding lands. Grain and coin flow upward, and the complaints flow with them.
districts.name: Manor Houses District

districts.flavor: Villages dot the countryside beyond the town walls, each with its own fields and well. The peasants here grow the food that the town takes for granted.
districts.name: Villages District

districts.flavor: In these feasting halls, the tribe gathers to eat, drink, and boast of its deeds. The stories grow a little taller with every cup.
districts.name: Feast Halls District

districts.flavor: The warriors of the tribe sharpen their weapons in these lodges and trade tales of past raids. The young listen closely, already planning raids of their own.
districts.name: War Lodges District

districts.flavor: The people gather in these open halls to air their grievances before the elders, and the elders, in turn, make sure the chief hears them too.
districts.name: Wantilans District

districts.flavor: The forests here provide timber for houses, ships, and fires, and the right to cut them is fiercely guarded. Stealing wood is punished almost as harshly as poaching deer.
focus: Possible production: Glass, Lacquerware & Cured Meat
districts.name: Forestry District

districts.flavor: Grain is the backbone of any economy, and the fields of this district grow it in plenty. What is not baked into bread is brewed, distilled, or sold.
districts.name: Grain Growing District

districts.flavor: Flocks of sheep graze the pastures of this district, and their wool is sold by the sack to weavers across the realm. More than one great merchant fortune began with a single flock.
focus: Possible production: Textiles, Leather, Cheese, Books & Paper & Medicaments
districts.name: Sheep Rearing District

districts.flavor: Cattle graze the pastures of this district, prized for their meat, their milk, and their strength at the plow. In many places, a bride's dowry is still counted in cows.
focus: Possible production: Cured Meat, Cheese & Leather
districts.name: Cattle Rearing District

districts.flavor: White cotton bolls ripen across the fields of this district, picked by hand and sold by the bale. Some far-off peoples believe it grows on plants that sprout tiny sheep.
districts.name: Cotton Growing District

districts.flavor: Quarries scar the hills of this district, where stone is cut for walls, temples, and castles across the realm. Some of its finest buildings began as a hillside here.
districts.name: Quarry District

districts.flavor: Fish from this district are eaten fresh, salted, smoked, or dried, and traded far inland where water is scarce. A good catch can feed a village for a month.
districts.name: Fishing District

districts.flavor: The vineyards of this district grow grapes for the table, for drying, and above all for wine. A good vintage is remembered for decades, and a bad one for even longer.
districts.name: Vineyard District

districts.flavor: Oil from this district lights lamps, cooks meals, anoints the faithful, and softens the skin of the rich. There is little it cannot do, and few households go without it.
districts.name: Olive Growing District

districts.flavor: Flooded paddies step across the land here, tended by entire villages who plant, weed, and harvest together. Growing rice is too much work for any family alone.
districts.name: Rice Growing District

requirements.name: County can produce Rice or Wetlands or Cultural tradition

options.detail: The Rice Growing District may be constructed in Wetlands
options.name: Cultural tradition

districts.flavor: Fields of millet and sorghum cover the dry plains here, tall enough to hide a rider. Their small, hard grains keep for years without spoiling.
districts.name: Millet Growing District

districts.flavor: Whatever lies beneath this district, be it iron, silver, or salt, is dug out by miners who spend more of their lives underground than above it.
districts.name: Mining District

requirements.name: County can produce Iron or County can produce Copper or County can produce Gold or County can produce Silver or County can produce Gems or County can produce Alum or County can produce Jade or County can produce Salt

districts.flavor: Without salt there is no preserving meat or fish through the lean months, and no keeping an army fed. This district supplies a great deal of it, and knows it.
districts.name: Salt Harvesting District

districts.flavor: Amber washes up here after storms and is dug from the sands and marshes inland. A piece with an insect trapped inside is thought to bring luck.
districts.name: Amber Harvesting District

districts.flavor: The silk of this district begins as tiny worms, fed on mulberry leaves day and night. A single robe takes the cocoons of thousands of them.
districts.name: Silk Growing District

districts.flavor: Trappers from this district go out in the coldest months, when the animals' fur is thickest and most valuable. A single fine pelt can be worth a season's wages.
districts.name: Furrier District

districts.flavor: Spices here come from every part of a plant: bark, buds, berries, roots, or the threads of a flower. All of it is gathered by hand and dried with care.
districts.name: Spice Growing District

districts.flavor: Tea bushes grow on the steep hillsides of this district, where mist hangs in the mornings. The finest leaves are picked young, a single bud and two leaves at a time.
districts.name: Tea Growing District

districts.flavor: The dyes of this district come from roots, leaves, berries, and even crushed insects. A deep, lasting color can take a dozen soakings to achieve.
districts.name: Dyemaking District

districts.flavor: Elephants in this district are captured, tamed, and trained for war, work, and worship. Their ivory is only part of their value.
districts.name: Ivory Hunting District

districts.flavor: Sugar cane grows tall in this district and is crushed for its sweet juice, which is boiled down into hard loaves. Far away, a single loaf is worth more than a cow.
districts.name: Sugar Growing District

districts.flavor: The incense of this district is resin bled from the bark of trees and left to harden in the sun. Its smoke rises in temples across the known world.
districts.name: Incense Harvesting District

districts.flavor: Medicinal herbs grow in the gardens and wild places of this district, gathered by people who know which leaves heal and which ones harm.
districts.name: Medicinal Plant Harvesting District

districts.flavor: The clay of this district is so fine that potters travel for weeks to dig it. The best pieces fired here ring like a bell when tapped.
districts.name: Ceramics Making District

districts.flavor: Fields of hemp cover this district, cut, soaked, and beaten for the fibers that become rope, cloth, and canvas.
districts.name: Hemp Growing District

districts.flavor: Flax is pulled up by the roots here rather than cut, so that every inch of fiber is saved. Its seeds are pressed, and the pressings fed to the animals.
districts.name: Flax Growing District

districts.flavor: Bees are kept here in hives of straw, clay, or hollow logs, and calmed with smoke when the honey is taken. For most people, it is the only sweetness they ever taste.
districts.name: Apiary District

districts.flavor: Orchards of fruit trees cover the slopes and valleys of this district, and their fruit is eaten fresh, dried in the sun, or pressed.
districts.name: Fruit Harvesting District

districts.flavor: Open pastures, paddocks, and stables fill this district, where horses are bred, broken, and sold to riders from across the realm.
districts.name: Horse Rearing District

districts.flavor: The Holy Site in this area attracts Christian pilgrims from all around the known world. The grand basilica is not just a marvel of engineering and beauty, but also a safe haven for travelers and a prestigious monument to its sponsor.
districts.name: Grand Basilica

districts.flavor: The Holy Site in this area is a popular destination for devout pilgrims. The grand mosque gives them a place to pray, rest and pay homage before continuing their journey. Its beautiful domes and great intricate spires signal the greatness of god for all to see.
districts.name: Grand Mosque

districts.flavor: Inside this grand edifice burns an Atash Behram, a Fire of Victory, the greatest and purest of all flames, gathered from lightning, royal candles, cremation pyres, goldsmiths' furnaces and ascetics' hearths. Pilgrims from far away lands come to behold this wonder, while the magi perform seemingly unending purification rites.
districts.name: Great Fire Temple

districts.flavor: The Holy Site in this area attracts the faithful in droves. The grand temple is covered in ornate carvings displaying heroic deeds by gods and demi-gods alike. Massive bonfires send plumes of smoke upwards to the gods themselves, with holy men administering blessings to all who venerate the spirits.
districts.name: Grand Temple

districts.flavor: The Holy Site in this area attracts scores of humble pilgrims seeking to cleanse their souls. The grand temple is covered from foundation to spire with statues and idols to the gods, retelling ancient legends and the lives of noble prophets.
districts.name: Grand Temple

districts.flavor: The Holy Site in this area attracts scores of humble pilgrims seeking to cleanse their souls. At the center of the complex is a grand Stupa, home to a number of Relics of the Buddha himself.
districts.name: Grand Temple

districts.flavor: The Holy Site in this area is a meeting point for the devout and dedicated. An impressive roof makes up as much as half of the main temple building and can be seen from afar. Inside a great single hall can house as many pious visitors as needed.
districts.name: Grand Shrine

districts.flavor: The Holy Site in this area is a focal point for believers. Palatial temple buildings and pagodas in symbolic colors are arranged in harmony around a symmetrical courtyard. The balanced layout of the compound radiates peaceful reverence.
districts.name: Grand Temple

districts.flavor: The Holy Site in this area is a meeting point for the devout and dedicated. The grand temple stands as a noble tribute to the higher powers, its walls and domes smoothed and painted in resplendent colors that honor the divine.
districts.name: Grand Temple

districts.flavor: The Holy Site in this area is a meeting point for the devout and dedicated. The grand temple stands as a noble tribute to the higher powers, its walls and domes smoothed and painted in resplendent colors that honor the divine.
districts.name: Grand Temple

districts.flavor: The Mahabodhi Temple marks the location where the Buddha is said to have attained enlightenment. The site is a significant destination for pilgrimage by both Buddhists and Hindus. The construction of the temple was started around the year 200 by Emperor Ashoka, and has since been improved and restored multiple times.
districts.name: Mahabodhi Temple

districts.flavor: The Imam Ali Mosque houses the tomb of Ali, cousin of Muhammad and the first Shi'ite Imam after him. Thousands of pilgrims come to pay tribute each year, greeted by the magnificent green dome of the mosque.
districts.name: Imam Ali Mosque

districts.flavor: The Great Mosque of Mecca is a massive and ancient structure whose walls surround the holy Kaaba. Many great Sultans have expanded upon the mosque and its surroundings since its construction. Every Muslim is supposed to visit this site when on the Hajj.
districts.name: Great Mosque of Mecca

districts.flavor: The Great Mosque of Cordoba was erected after the Islamic Conquest of the Visigothic Kingdom, upon the foundation of a Christian church. Originally the site was shared, with both Muslims and Christians using it, but the Christian half was eventually purchased and demolished to make room for the Grand Mosque.
districts.name: The Great Mosque of Cordoba

districts.flavor: The Great Mosque of Djenne stands on the bank of the Bani River. Constructed entirely out of mudbrick it requires a lot of care, which the faithful are more than willing to provide. Every year, large gatherings of people converge to repair and improve the mosque.
districts.name: Great Mosque of Djenne

districts.flavor: The Great Mosque of Samarra was completed in AD 851 by the Abbasid caliph Al-Mutawakkil, who reigned in Samarra. Its most prominent feature is the Malwiya Tower, a magnificent spiral minaret, which towers towards the skies at an impressive height.
districts.name: Great Mosque of Samarra

districts.flavor: The Cologne Cathedral houses the relics of the Three Kings, which draw the attention of pilgrims from all over the Christian world. The cathedral is built using Gothic architecture and is richly adorned with spires and intricate details.
districts.name: Cologne Cathedral

districts.flavor: Augustine, Roman missionary and later archbishop, built the Canterbury Cathedral after choosing the town as his center for the episcopal see in Kent. This new cathedral revived the importance of the city, granting it authority over the English church.
districts.name: Canterbury Cathedral

districts.flavor: The Prophetic Mosque, or the Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, is an open-air style mosque established by the prophet Muhammad himself. It was one of the first mosques that he constructed, and the site was close to where he had his residence.
districts.name: The Prophetic Mosque

districts.flavor: The Doge's Palace acts as the residence for the government of the Republic of Venice. An impressive structure, it houses multiple chambers dedicated to things such as the Council, Senate, administration, and justice.
districts.name: Doge's Palace

districts.flavor: The Walls of Genoa were built in the 9th century after the city was granted significant autonomy. The walls, together with the protection of the coastline, allow the area to develop and prosper.
districts.name: Walls of Genoa

districts.flavor: The Visby City Wall protects the city from external threats such as raiders or Danes. It also efficiently keeps out tax collectors sent by the Thing of Gotland! To get to the riches within, assailants must first deal with a plethora of towers all manned by archers.
districts.name: Visby Ringmur

districts.flavor: The Walls of Benin are a massive series of earthworks (Iya in the Edo language), that encircle the entirety of Benin. The walls are built of a ditch and dike structure, with an inner moat and an exterior rampart.
districts.name: Walls of Benin

districts.flavor:
The Colosseum is one of the largest amphitheaters ever built and has hosted countless spectacles such as gladiatorial combat, animal hunts and even reconstructed sea battles. Its construction was started by the Roman emperor Vespasian in AD 72 and was completed in AD 80 under his successor, Titus.

Despite its vibrant history, its primary use today is for harvesting marble and bronze for use elsewhere.
districts.name: The Colosseum

districts.flavor: The mighty Iron Pillar of Delhi stands as a symbol to the glory of King Chandragupta II, though subsequent rulers have also etched their names into it. Despite having stood for a long time, there's no trace of rust – a testament to the skill of Indian ironsmiths!
districts.name: Iron Pillar of Delhi

districts.flavor: The Iron Pillar of Dhar is constructed from the molten-down arms of an entire army. The craftsmanship is truly astounding, bringing glory upon the dynasty which holds it.
districts.name: Iron Pillar of Dhar

districts.flavor: The pyramids, most prominently the one of Cheops, stand as wonders of the ancient world. Vast and impressive, they enhance the image of any ruler who controls them.
districts.name: The Pyramids

districts.flavor: Stonehenge is an ancient, mystical structure that has inspired many a scholar. Even today, in these enlightened times, learned men from all around Britain flock to study it. What truly is its purpose?
districts.name: Stonehenge

districts.flavor: Offa's Dyke, which is a long ditch flanked by a wall of earth, was constructed by the Anglo-Saxon king of Mercia to defend the border towards Wales. This raised earthwork offers an advantage to whoever stands on the side of the wall, as any attackers have to fight an uphill battle from the ditch.
districts.name: Offa's Dyke

districts.flavor: Hadrian's Wall was built during Roman times to keep the northern Picts out of the province of Britannia. Nowadays it serves no defensive purpose, but the stones make for a cheap and convenient source of building material!
districts.name: Hadrian's Wall

districts.flavor: The city of Petra is a true wonder of the ancient world. Carved directly out of naturally occurring rose-tinted rock, the city stands as a curiosity that intrigues even the mightiest sultan.
districts.name: Petra

districts.flavor: Carved out of the mountainside, the massive Buddhas of Bamian loom over any visitors. While the area surrounding them is no longer the thriving center of Buddhist learning as it once was, there's still numerous Buddhist pilgrims and scholars visiting the statues. A shrewd Dharmic ruler might even be able to pull a profit from the pilgrims, in addition to gaining some personal insights.
districts.name: Buddhas of Bamian

districts.flavor: The Alhambra is a fortress built upon the remains of an ancient Roman fortification. While it is serviceable as a defensive structure, with the right investments it could be turned into something more...
districts.name: Alhambra

districts.flavor: The Citadel of Aleppo is an ancient fortification, having been in use by numerous powers since it was constructed. The citadel acts as a royal residence, fortified retreat, temple and prison.
districts.name: Citadel of Aleppo

districts.flavor: The House of Wisdom contains a vast collection of books, and the scribes therein work tirelessly both day and night to translate even more great works of literature. The sources vary from Greek, Persian, Indian and many more — truly, it contains the entire world's knowledge! A shining beacon of human knowledge! And comfortably far from the illiterate horsemen of the steppe...
districts.name: House of Wisdom

districts.flavor: The Tower of London is a castle that serves as both a vital fortification and a prison. The central tower is called the 'White Tower' and houses the ruling class. The position of the Tower of London means that it's vital to the defense of the entire County.
districts.name: The Tower of London

districts.flavor: There have been bridges over the River Thames since time immemorial, but this one — made of mighty stone — stands grander than all prior. The churning currents below have led to the common acceptance that the bridge is for wise men to pass over, and for fools to pass under.
districts.name: London Bridge

districts.flavor:
Also known as 'Our Lady of Paris,' this magnificent cathedral is dedicated to the Virgin Mary. Constructed in the Gothic style, it impresses with numerous statues and enormous colorful rose windows.

On the outside, the cathedral is covered with sculptures vividly retelling biblical stories, allowing even illiterate peasants to understand the glory of God!
districts.name: Notre-Dame

districts.flavor: The Brihadeeswarar Temple is dedicated to the Hindu deity Shiva and is one of the largest South Indian temples built in the ornate Dravidian architectural style. The name of the temple is a Sanskrit composite word that roughly translates as "Temple of the Great Lord Shiva."
districts.name: Brihadeeswarar Temple

districts.flavor: The Shwedagon Pagoda is a sacred Buddhist stupa built by the Mon people around the year 500. It houses many famous relics, such as the staff of Kakusandha, the water filter of Koṇāgamana, a piece of the robe of Kassapa, and eight strands of hair from the head of Gautama.
districts.name: Shwedagon Pagoda

districts.flavor: While Pagan has thousands of pagodas, temples, and shrines littered throughout the city and the surrounding plains, the Ananda Temple stands as a crowning achievement among them. The perfectly dimensioned structure contains many unique plaques and stone images. It is a place of worship and a center of learning to educate the people in religious ethos.
districts.name: Ananda Temple

districts.flavor: The Friday Mosque, or the Jameh Mosque of Esfahan, was built during the Umayyad dynasty. It is said that the Caliph personally made one of the pillars in the mosque. Before becoming a mosque, it is said that it used to be a house of worship for Zoroastrians.
districts.name: The Friday Mosque

districts.flavor: The Khajuraho temples are dedicated to the coexistence between Hindus and Jains, where their diverse religious views are celebrated. The temple walls are covered with intricate art and sculptures, making the place truly resplendent and attractive to pilgrims and scholars alike.
districts.name: Temple City

districts.flavor: The Palace of Aachen was chosen by Charlemagne to be the center of power of the Carolingian Empire. It served a both political and religious purpose, and is still an excellent place for hosting important gatherings.
districts.name: Palace of Aachen

districts.flavor:
The Hagia Sophia is a true marvel of engineering, with a massive dome standing out as the most impressive feature. Completed in AD 537 by emperor Justinian I, it now houses the Ecumenical Patriarch and stands as a monument to Christianity.

And so it will remain for all eternity, for surely nothing could ever topple the might of Rome.
districts.name: Hagia Sophia

districts.flavor: The Dome of the Rock is situated in the center of the Temple Mount, in the place where the Temple of Solomon and the Jewish Second Temple stood. The temples foundation stone is said to be the place where God created the world and the first human, Adam. The Dome of the Rock and the nearby Church of the Holy Sepulchre attract Abrahamic pilgrims from all around the world.
districts.name: Temple in Jerusalem

districts.flavor: A grand hall where heroic warriors can meet and organize their next adventure.
districts.name: Hall of Heroes

districts.flavor: A university is a place of higher learning, reserved for those of good standing and wealth who are deemed worthy enough. It attracts scholars and scientists who debate, study, scribe, and ultimately pool their knowledge within its walls.
districts.name: University

districts.flavor:
A university is a place of higher learning, reserved for those of good standing and wealth who are deemed worthy enough. It attracts scholars and scientists who debate, study, scribe, and ultimately pool their knowledge within its walls.

The Al-Azhar University is named in honor of Fatimah, the daughter of Muhammad, who was often called 'al-Zahra' (the Luminous).
districts.name: Al-Azhar University

districts.flavor:
A university is a place of higher learning, reserved for those of good standing and wealth who are deemed worthy enough. It attracts scholars and scientists who debate, study, scribe, and ultimately pool their knowledge within its walls.

The University of Sankoré, which started out as a Mosque, transformed into a center of learning after acquiring a wealth of books from traveling merchants.
districts.name: The University of Sankoré

districts.flavor:
A university is a place of higher learning, reserved for those of good standing and wealth who are deemed worthy enough. It attracts scholars and scientists who debate, study, scribe, and ultimately pool their knowledge within its walls.

The University of Siena and the maestri who serve within are entirely funded by taxes from Siena itself, more specifically a tax imposed on those who rents rooms to its students.
districts.name: The University of Siena

districts.flavor:
A university is a place of higher learning, reserved for those of good standing and wealth who are deemed worthy enough. It attracts scholars and scientists who debate, study, scribe, and ultimately pool their knowledge within its walls.

The Nalanda University is an important seat of Vedic scholarship and attracts students from as far away as Tibet and China.
districts.name: Nalanda University

districts.flavor: Representatives of the Three Estates meet regularly at this building to deliberate on the affairs of the realm and advice the current ruler.
districts.name: Parliament

districts.flavor: This building is seemingly excellent for growing vegetables.
districts.name: Glass Monument

districts.flavor: Hotin Fort is a small fort built on the banks of the river Dniester. Its location allows it to protect local trade routes and grants the owner control of the river.
districts.name: Hotin Fortification

districts.flavor: Modeled and named after a gate in Constantinople, the Golden Gate of Kyiv serves as both an entrance to the city and a triumphal arch. The golden dome of the church, built on top of the gate, can be seen from afar and makes it a prominent symbol of Kyiv.
districts.name: Golden Gate of Kyiv

districts.flavor: Heddal Stave Church is the largest stave church in Norway and has a beautiful wooden interior. Legend says the church was built by a mountain troll in merely three days.
districts.name: Heddal Stave Church

districts.flavor: The temple at Uppsala serves as a religious center for large parts of Scandinavia. A sacred tree stands near the temple, next to a well, similar to that of the legendary Yggdrasil.
districts.name: Temple of Uppsala

districts.flavor: Lund Cathedral is a magnificent church richly decorated with stone sculptures. Constructed with influences from Romanesque architecture, the church shares a lot of similarities with churches in Germany. The building is dedicated to Saint Lawrence, who is the patron saint of Lund.
districts.name: Lund Cathedral

districts.flavor: The Danevirke is an extensive earthwork fortification built to prevent incursions from the continent into Danish territories and has been expanded multiple times since its original construction.
districts.name: Danevirke

districts.flavor: Built by the Romans long ago, the great Walls of Lugo remain an impressive sight. Pilgrims pass their five gates on the road to Santiago de Compostela, making the journey even more profound.
districts.name: Roman Walls of Lugo

districts.flavor: The monolithic Rock of Gibraltar overlooks a narrow strait that is the gateway to the Mediterranean Sea. It was one of the Pillars of Hercules in antiquity, considered to mark the end of the known world. Looking at it now, you cannot help but wonder what lies beyond.
districts.name: Rock of Gibraltar

districts.flavor: A great palace-fortress built on the Saría plain, the Aljafería is a testament to the power and wealth of Zaragoza. Imposing and splendid in equal measure; it is both an intimidating fortification and a pinnacle of Iberian architecture.
districts.name: Aljafería

districts.flavor: This ancient lighthouse is said to have been based on its more famous sister in Alexandria. Having guided seafarers for untold centuries, it remains important to Galicia's coastal trade. Some claim that you can glimpse Ireland's green coast from the top of this lonely tower, but gazing out, you see only endless sea.
districts.name: Farum Brigantium

districts.flavor: Originally built by the Romans in days of old, these massive walls were significantly expanded under the reign of Wamba, king of the Visigoths. The early Arabic rulers widened them even further, creating a defensive system fit for the City of Kings.
districts.name: City Walls of Toledo

districts.flavor: Rising like the bow of a ship from a rocky crag, this fortress is an awe-inspiring sight. As majestic as it is impenetrable, it is the greatest of all castles in the kingdom of castles — Castile.
districts.name: Alcázar of Segovia

districts.flavor: Built over the tomb of James the Great, this splendid edifice is the end point of the Way of Saint James, and the crown of one of the great sites of Christendom. Pilgrims from all over Western and Northern Europe arrive in large numbers, speaking dozens of tongues — though many become mute with awe.
districts.name: Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela

districts.flavor: This sanctuary houses the remains of Ali ar-Rida, celebrated by some Shiites as the eighth imam, who was martyred in this land. The ever-expanding complex includes his shrine as well as prayer halls, a library and a bazaar, growing in an eclectic but glorious fashion with the ebb and flow of pilgrims and caravans.
districts.name: Sanctuary of Imam Reza

districts.flavor: Both temple and mausoleum, the grand scale and exquisite symmetry of this building is sure to inspire many great works yet to come. Its great double-shelled dome is clad in turquoise, and of such a scale that it almost seems like a challenge to heaven.
districts.name: Dome of Soltaniyeh

districts.flavor: This ancient edifice was the ceremonial seat of the Sasanian kings of kings, but silence has fallen over its once glorious halls, and the flowers in the gardens bloom no more. Much material was taken for the founding of Baghdad, and the people have scattered to the four winds. Yet, an eerie splendor remains, the lingering glory of old.
districts.name: Ruins of the Palace of Ctesiphon

primaryBuilding.name: Ruins of the Palace of Ctesiphon

districts.flavor: Ensconced on a hilltop above the town of Khorramabad, this Sasanian mudbrick fortress remains an impressive sight. The inhabitants of the valley call it Falak-ol-Aflak, "The Heaven of Heavens", for it seems to them to rest on top of the world, and within its strong walls, they have often found refuge.
districts.name: Falak-ol-Aflak

districts.flavor: This structure towers over the Hari river valley, covered in stucco and glazed tile decorations and alternating bands of calligraphy, an exquisite monument to what faith and wealth can achieve even in these remote, rugged lands.
districts.name: Minaret of Jam

districts.flavor: A vast fortification system built by the ancient kings as a bulwark against the Hephthalites Huns, the Great Wall of Gorgan is shrouded in legend. Alexander the Great himself is said to have passed through its gates on his march to conquer the East.
districts.name: Great Wall of Gorgan

districts.flavor: Though this seasonal lake is sometimes merely a dry salt flat, in mid-summer the waters achieve an exquisite, pale red hue. Young poets gather at the shore to gaze upon the strange water, and ponder the beauty and mysteries of the earth.
districts.name: Lake Maharloo

districts.flavor: The Creator themselves seem to have painted these ridges in a rainbow of colors. Bands of red, white, yellow, gray, orange and yet stranger hues tint the rocky, tranquil landscape. Local rulers will often take guest hunting here, to see this sublime wonder.
districts.name: Rainbow Mountains

districts.flavor: A great, snow-capped pinnacle steeped in ancient lore, Mount Damavand is said to be the prison of the monstrous tyrant Zahhāk, where he will abide until the end of the world. Many heroes of old have performed great feats on this mountain, and to those who travel there today, its mighty presence seem to touch their very souls. A dormant volcano, its slopes are dotted by hot springs where weary travelers can stop and relax, pondering the deeds of the ancients.
districts.name: Mount Damavand

districts.flavor: This ancient tomb of white limestone is said to be the resting place of Batsheba, the mother of king Solomon, exalted by many faiths. Women tend to the site, and only women are allowed to enter the tomb's dark interior. They seldom speak of what they have seen inside. The waters nearby are said to be blessed, and can cure those who have been bitten by mad dogs.
districts.name: Tomb of Batsheba

districts.flavor: It is said that prince Siyavusha built this massive fortress when the world was young. Three thousand years later, it was restored by the Bukhara Khudas, the ancient rulers of this region, and it has been in use ever since. Travelers come from near and far to admire the construction, with seven great pillars mirroring the seven stars of the Big Dipper, but it is a fortification first and foremost, intimidating in its splendor.
districts.name: Ark of Bukhara

districts.flavor: The name of this tomb complex means The Living King, referring to Muhammad's cousin Quham ibn Abbas who is said to be buried here. The mausoleums are quite small and humble, yet they hold a solemn beauty that makes many linger amidst the silent tombs, to ponder the transience of life.
districts.name: Shah-i-Zinda

districts.flavor: This eagle's nest, perched atop a lofty crag, was built by the Justanids to serve as a fortress redoubt of their beleaguered realm. With its awe-inspiring setting and strong ramparts, it is near-impregnable by all accounts, and could prove an ideal stronghold for any warlike faction or sect that would thrive in such an isolated location.
districts.name: Alamut Castle

districts.flavor: Perched atop a lofty crag, this castle has long served as a remote mountain redoubt. It has now been rebuilt into a formidable fedayeen fortress, housing libraries, laboratories and tranquil gardens among the imposing fortifications. To some, it is a place of bloodshed and war, to others a place of spiritual repose - or perhaps both.
districts.name: Hashshashin Castle IV

districts.flavor: Built in a quiet part of the duchy, this flat, open-topped tower is where the locals lay their dead to rest. Bodies inside are exposed to carrion birds and the rigors of the sun, conveying their departed souls safely to the afterlife and keeping the living free of corruption. Religious proscriptions necessitate the tower rather than the traditional wilderness, but its presence binds the community fast.
districts.name: Tower of Silence

districts.flavor:
The Holy Cross has long conquered this magnificent structure, vanquishing the pagan cult to the virgin goddess Athena.
Nowadays, it holds the shrines to Maria Parthenos, Mother of God and only Virgin worthy of the name Holy.
districts.name: Temple of the Theotokos

districts.flavor:
The church of Saint Demetrios is the most important shrine in the city.
First raised when the faith in Christ was still young, it incorporates the Roman bathhouse in which the Saint, together with many other early believers, was imprisoned, martyrized, and buried.
districts.name: Hagios Demetrios

districts.flavor: An imposing fortification on the coast. Its strategic position overseeing the channel separating the island from the mainland makes it a vital control point in the Ionian area.
districts.name: Kassiopi Castle

districts.flavor:
According to tradition, Lazarus of Bethany, once raised from the dead by Christ, was buried in the town of Larnaca upon his second death.
The tomb was lost for centuries but, upon its retrieval, Emperor Leo VI had the saint's remains moved to Constantinople and this imposing church built on top of the grave.
districts.name: Church of Saint Lazarus

districts.flavor:
The origins of this monastery, built on a steep cliff on the Black Mountain, are so remote to be almost shrouded in mystery; according to some, it was first erected by order of Emperor Theodosius in the 4th century, but the sacred spring and ancient frescoes could be even older.
The monastery's gem is a fresco of the Mother of God, said to have been painted by Apostle Luke himself.
districts.name: Sumela Monastery

districts.flavor:
The archaic acropolis of the city of Patras, rising on a hill of the Vodias mountains, was replaced by a fortification during the reign of Emperor Justinian.
The castle has been uninterruptedly in use since then, always under the protection of the local patron, St. Andrew, and of the genius loci Patrinella, the Roman statue of a maiden.
districts.name: Patras Castle

districts.flavor:
This rock in front of the coast already hosted a custom station at the times of Alcibiades the Athenian thanks to its ideal position at the entrance of the Bosphorus strait.
A fortified tower on the same small island is now able to control all naval traffic coming from and heading to the Black Sea; in addition, a large chain can be lifted to the sea level between the tower and Constantinople, effectively blocking the passage to any dangerous or unwanted ship.
districts.name: Maiden's Tower

districts.flavor:
A grandiose palace in a safe location on Mt. Taygetos, just above the fortified city of Mystras.
The palace has all the luxuries to compete with the greatness of the Constantinopolitan halls, and it's worthy of only the richest and most influential of governors.
districts.name: Despots' Palace

districts.flavor: Meteora is the name given by the locals to a breathtaking rock formation made of natural pillars rising just beside Mount Pidnos.
districts.name: Meteora

districts.flavor: According to tradition, the Virgin Mary was sailing from Palestine to Cyprus to visit her son's friend, Lazarus, who was evangelizing the island, when the ship was blown off-course and forced to land here, by Mount Athos. When Mary disembarked, she was in awe of the natural beauty of the area, so she blessed it and asked for it as her own garden. A voice from Heaven granted her wish; since then, the area is considered holy and is forbidden to any other woman.
districts.name: Mount Athos

districts.flavor:
The Basilica of Sant'Apollinare Nuovo has only gained its current name recently, when the relics of Saint Apollinaris were transferred from the neighboring Basilica in Classe. Its history, however, is much longer.
First consecrated in the early 6th century by King Theodoric of the Ostrogoths as an Arian church, the building has seen many renovations both in structure and decoration while maintaining its unique style — an elegant mixture of western and eastern art — and its amazing Byzantine mosaics.
districts.name: Sant'Apollinare Nuovo

districts.flavor:
An unassuming monastery in the middle of the desert, but with a heavy history. The first monastic structure was, in fact, ordered to be built by Emperor Constantine's mother on the site of the apparition of the Burning Bush to Moses. Emperor Justinian financed its expansion into the current fortified monastery, also enclosing the Well of Moses. Only centuries after its foundation did the spoils of Saint Catherine arrive at the monastery, changing its name.
The monastery has always been among the most ancient and prolific scriptoria and icon-making centers.
districts.name: Saint Catherine's Monastery

districts.flavor:
An ancient monastery erected on the exact spot where Saint Nino planted a miraculous cross while evangelizing Georgia.
The holy building attracts pilgrims from all over the Caucasus.
districts.name: Jvari Monastery

districts.flavor:
This ancient cathedral is the historical center of Armenian Apostolic Christianity. Originally founded by Saint Gregory the Illuminator over a pagan temple to symbolize the triumph of the newly-adopted religion of the Kingdom of Armenia, the church was destructed almost completely during the Sasanid invasion, and rebuilt from the ground some years later.
After the 7th century, however, the cathedral has been repeatedly plundered and abandoned, and has fallen into a state of disrepair. Only a drastic and expensive intervention could return it to its previous splendor.
districts.name: Cathedral of Vagarshapat

districts.flavor:
The Byzantine influence on this building is strong: a small church with baptistery, in red bricks nested upon naked rocks, with an "inscribed cross" plan and a rich decoration of fresco cycles, dominating the valley of the Stilaro stream.
The church is an isolated gem in the middle of hostile nature, where man can feel closer to God.
districts.name: Cattolica di Stilo

districts.flavor:
The monastery is dedicated to the preservation of the relics of Venerable Luke of Steiris, the hermit monk.
The holy remains are said to exude a miraculous oil, and attract countless pilgrims who sleep by the tomb in order to be healed by incubation. The inner decoration is praised throughout the Eastern Mediterranean for its quality and lavishness, as the finest artists of the age have enriched it with mosaics, icons, chandeliers, carvings, and cloths.
districts.name: Hosios Loukas

districts.flavor:
The cathedral of Ohrid was first destroyed when the Slavs first descended into these lands, and was not rebuilt until the area was safely back into the folds of the Christian faith.
Its last embodiment is a dome basilica richly decorated with fresco cycles from the finest artists of the age.
districts.name: Church of Saint Sophia

districts.flavor:
Rocks are extremely malleable in this area, naturally forming cones, peaks, and caves.
Humans have taken advantage of these structures for centuries, building stables, storage, and refuges, then houses and production buildings, then finally churches inside the rock cones, and whole settlements have thus formed.
districts.name: Troglodytic Settlements

districts.flavor:
The Cilician Gates are a pass through the Taurus Mountains that connect the Cilician plains with the Anatolian plateau.
Since time immemorial, the pass has been fortified, and controlling it meant controlling one of the main commercial and military arteries of Asia Minor and the Middle East.
districts.name: Cilician Gates

districts.flavor: A Mongolian palace, serving both as a military and cultural center in equal measure. Its crowning glory stands as a fountain in the shape of a silver tree, where different kinds of wine flow from the serpents that entwine the statue.
districts.name: Pleasure Dome

districts.flavor:
The Burkhan Khaldun is the most imposing of the Khentii Mountains.
Said to be the birthplace of many Mongolian heroes, its slopes are covered in ovoos and many sacrifices are made in the hopes of gaining its favor.
districts.name: Burkhan Khaldun

districts.flavor: The reefs, beaches, and mangrove forests of Pemba Island provide an abundance of inlets and resources for the people of Pemba, making it a natural entrepôt of the Zanj.
districts.name: Pemba Trade Ports

districts.flavor: The island of Unguja's sandy shores sheltered by coral islets make it a perfect haven for ships. Traders from across the Indian Ocean come to enjoy Unguja's natural strengths as a center of maritime commerce.
districts.name: Zanzibar Trade Ports

districts.flavor: Perched atop a rocky island surrounded by steep cliffs, Mombasa enjoys a naturally defensible position that still remains uniquely accessible to maritime traffic.
districts.name: Port of Mombasa

districts.flavor: Located on the northern edge of the Swahili heartlands, Pate Island was one of the first Swahili regions introduced to Islam and thus to Middle Eastern trade networks.
districts.name: Pate Island Trade Ports

districts.flavor: The warm white sands of its beaches and the vibrant blue of the waters that lazily lap its shores belie the bustling commerce that serves as the lifeblood of Lamu. Long connected to trade across the ocean, goods from the western and eastern ends of the known world can be bought and sold here.
districts.name: Lamu Trade Ports

districts.flavor: These mountains are filled with thousands of imposing sandstone pillars rising high above the ground. While the pillars are the most striking feature, the area is also filled with ravines, streams, small lakes and caves.
districts.name: Wulingyuan

districts.flavor: Carved into the side of a cliff, this Buddha statue faces the confluence of the Min and Dadu rivers, greeting weary travelers on their journey.
districts.name: Leshan Giant Buddha

districts.flavor: A large complex of temple grottoes, containing a several dozen of larger caves and hundreds of smaller ones. The caves are filled with thousands upon thousands of Buddha statues.
districts.name: Yungang Grottoes

districts.flavor: The Wudang mountains are one of several mountains sacred to Taoism. They are also the home to large temple complex, famed for the practice of tai chi.
districts.name: Wudang Mountain Temples

districts.flavor: The Shaolin Monastery is perhaps most famous for being the birthplace of Shaolin kung fu and for producing monks highly skilled in martial arts. It is, however, also a place of learning and study, and for translating Buddhist texts.
districts.name: Shaolin Monastery

districts.flavor: Lingyin Temple was founded by an Indian monk and pilgrim in 328 AD to spread Buddhism. Since then, the temple has grown immensely. It has several pavilions, a large number of grottoes and pagodas, and has enough dormitories to house thousands of monks.
districts.name: Lingyin Temple

districts.flavor: The Giant Wild Goose Pagoda was originally constructed in 652 AD as a place to keep and conserve texts, carvings, and various figurines. It was later rebuilt to have an impressive ten stories, until various reconstructions and restorations lowered it to seven stories.
districts.name: Giant Wild Goose Pagoda

districts.flavor: The imperial palace in Kaifeng was built when the Song dynasty established its capital in the city. A strong and efficient government rule within these walls, ensuring that the city and the realm at large will prosper.
districts.name: Kaifeng Imperial Palace

districts.flavor: The Forbidden City is a vast imperial palace, consisting of almost a thousand separate buildings. The entire compound is surrounded by a high wall and a deep moat, protecting the ruling government and the many officials working tirelessly within.
districts.name: The Forbidden City

districts.flavor: The Qianling Mausoleum is primarily the tomb of Emperor Gaozong and Empress Wu Zetian, though several other members of the Li family is buried here as well. The burial mound is protected by a rectangular wall and the many stone statues that adorn the landscape is one of the mausoleum's most recognizable features.
districts.name: Qianling Mausoleum

districts.flavor: Quanzhou's port attracts foreign merchants from far and wide. Traders are known to come from Arabia and Anatolia, Japan and Korea, and everything in-between. This influx of trade vessels ensures that local industries are booming and it has made Quanzhou the foremost shipbuilder in the region.
districts.name: Quanzhou Seaport

districts.flavor: Angkor Wat is a massive temple complex dedicated to the deity Vishnu. It is designed to be a representation of Mount Meru, home of the gods in Hindu mythology. The complex is surrounded by an impressive moat and has several galleried temples, overflowing with religious art, sculptures and reliefs.
districts.name: Angkor Wat

districts.flavor: A citadel that serves as a military base for local armies and is greatly fortified to help repel invaders.
districts.name: Citadel of Thăng Long

districts.flavor: A pinnacle of Cham architecture, the Po Klong Garai temple is said to be built to honor the legendary king of the same name. It has three distinct brick towers and an impressive sculpture of the god Shiva as its primary art piece.
districts.name: Po Klong Garai Temple

districts.flavor: Krakatoa is a imposing volcano situated on a small archipelago just off the coast.
districts.name: Krakatoa

districts.flavor: Borobudur is a massive Buddhist temple consisting of nine stone platforms stacked on top of each other, topped by a central dome. The temple is decorated with thousands of reliefs and hundreds of Buddha statues.
districts.name: Borobudur

districts.flavor: Hōshi Ryokan is an old traditional inn and a family business. It offers travelers a respite on their journey with rest, food, and access to hot spring baths.
districts.name: Hōshi Ryokan

districts.flavor: The bustling markets of Herat have been renowned since the ancient Achaemenids it Haraiva. The caravans that enter and leave the city every day mark the bazaars of Herat as the Pearl of Khorasan.
districts.name: Bazaar of Herat

districts.flavor: The venerable market of Tabriz has served as the great hub of commerce since time immemorial. Its walls are decorated with colorful tiles and tinted plasters, reflecting the wealth and prestige of this ancient marketplace.
districts.name: Bazaar of Tabriz

districts.flavor: At a prime crossroads between India and China, the merchants of Lhasa crowd for traveler's attention in the shadow of the lofty Potala palace.
districts.name: Khrom of Lhasa

districts.flavor: Gateway to the Steppe, the bustling city of Gurganj is notable for its abundance of traders and travelers seeking profits or fortune on the frontier.
districts.name: Bazaar of Gurganj

districts.flavor: The markets of the great city of Cháng'ān, Perpetual Peace, bustle with all manner of trade, and are an essential stop for nearly all commerce heading both in and out of China.
districts.name: Market of Cháng'ān

districts.flavor: The old town of Lahur was built around two major markets, surrounded by homes, all enclosed by a long mud wall. This bustling cluster of markets has hummed with activity as long as anyone can remember, and will likely hum with activity for generations to come.
districts.name: Bazaar of Lahur

districts.flavor: The heartland of the ancient Median people, Hamadan has been a center of commerce since the time of clay tablets and cuneiform inscriptions. Hundreds of generations of merchants have peddled their wares and worked their craft among the stalls of Hamadan's main bazaar.
districts.name: Hamadan Bazaar

districts.flavor: Sat on the glistening banks of the Shule river, the city of Dūnhuáng marks the gateway between the Hexi Corridor and the Tarim basin, and is a key stopping point for all travelers between them.
districts.name: Market of Dūnhuáng

districts.flavor: Some locals will tell you that before there was money, Kashgar already had the Sunday Bazaar. Walking between the stalls of the market, it certainly feels that way — it's impossible to imagine a time without this place.
districts.name: Sunday Bazaar

districts.flavor: The lone, towering, snow-capped peak of Fujisan marks the passage into eastern Japan and is a sight famed throughout the islands, drawing travelers and pilgrims, and granting repose to all who gaze upon it. Among the most sacred Shintō mountains, Fuji is home to Konohanasakuya-hime, goddess of volcanoes, the cherry blossom, and life's ephemeral delicacy.
districts.name: Mount Fuji

districts.flavor: Established in the 6th century and dedicated to the Shintō goddesses of the sea and storms, Itsukushima-jinja's galleries stand over the water, looking towards a famed torii gate which appears to float over the waters of Matsushima bay.
districts.name: Itsukushima Shrine

districts.flavor: Built by Emperor Kanmu as the centerpiece of his great city of Heian-kyō, or 'Peace Capital', the sprawling palace complex houses the imperial court, residence, and the central bureaucratic offices of Japan. Its corridors are bustling hubs of ceremony, politics, and intrigue, where ancient aristocratic families vie for influence.
districts.name: Heian Palace

districts.flavor: Ise-jingū is sacred to the sun goddess, Amaterasu, and among the most hallowed Shintō sites. The shrine houses the Yamato imperial regalia, and is overseen by a vestal Saigū priestess, chosen from among the imperial dynasty.
districts.name: Ise Shrine

districts.flavor: Dating to the 7th century, Kōfuku-ji is one of the Seven Great Temples of Nara, among the oldest and most important centers of Buddhist thought and power in Japan.
districts.name: Kōfuku Temple

districts.flavor: Founded by Saichō in the late 8th century, Enryaku-ji sits on Mount Hiei overlooking Emperor Kanmu's capital, Heian-kyō, and is the center of Japanese Pundarika, or Tendai, Buddhism in Japan.
districts.name: Enryaku Temple

districts.flavor: The town of Dazaifu is the imperial court's administrative center on distant Kyūshū. Established to oversee the island's defense, facilitate overseas trade, and host foreign dignitaries, governorship of Dazaifu is a common career stepping stone of ambitious bureaucrats.
districts.name: Dazaifu Office

districts.flavor: Originally based in Taga, the Chinjufu is the fortified center of the imperial pacification efforts in northern Japan, overseen by a special commander with responsibility for the region's defense and taxation.
districts.name: Chinjufu District

districts.flavor: Since the earliest days of the Yamato, the port city of Hakata on Kyūshū's northern shore has been a naval gateway, a bustling nexus overseen by the nearby Dazaifu office, where traders sell goods from far-off lands and diplomatic delegations step onto Japan's shores.
districts.name: Hakata Port

districts.flavor: Completed in the 7th century, Hwangnyongsa, or the 'Imperial Dragon Temple', is a sprawling complex built by King Jin-heung of Silla as a center of Buddhist teaching and power, and boasts one of the world's tallest pagodas.
districts.name: Hwangnyong Temple

districts.flavor: Situated just west of Gaeseong city at the mouth of the Ryeseong river, the port of Byeokran is the most direct route for foreign goods and travelers to enter the Korean peninsula, avoiding the northern borders and mountain ranges.
districts.name: Byeokran Port

districts.flavor: The lofty peak of Mount Baekdu is said to be the origin of all the mountains of the Korean peninsula, and its heights are a sacred place among the region's many faiths and peoples.
districts.name: Mount Baekdu

districts.flavor: A revered temple in Luy Lâu, marks the spot where monks from far-off lands first came together. The brick tower, relics, and mummified masters that remain there embody centuries of devotion to Buddhism.
districts.name: Dâu Temple

districts.flavor: A towering pagoda raised by kings to calm the tides and honor the Buddha. Its beacon shines over the land, a symbol of harmony between man and Heaven.
districts.name: Liuhe Pagoda

districts.flavor: Located along the Batang Hari River, Muaro Jambi's extensive brick compounds protected both trade and faith. As a Srivijayan stronghold, it provided refuge for rulers and mobilized armies within the Sumatran heartland.
districts.name: Muaro Jambi Compounds

districts.flavor: The Hanging Temple is a monastery suspended from a cliff face at Mount Heng. According to legend, its construction began centuries ago with a monk named Liaoran. Its wooden halls, built on stilts, contain shrines to Buddhist, Taoist, and Confucian sages, blending faiths and defying gravity with graceful serenity.
districts.name: Hanging Temple

districts.flavor: The Pagoda of Fogong Temple is a tall wooden pagoda built without nails. Rising nine stories, it houses sacred relics and statues, and its clever design remains a marvel of engineering and a symbol of faith.
districts.name: Pagoda of Fogong Temple

districts.flavor: The Plain of Jars is a vast plateau strewn with giant stone vessels, their purpose shrouded in mystery. Once used in ancient rites, they endure as relics of a forgotten people, inspiring awe and local reverence.
districts.name: Plain of Jars

districts.flavor: The Dieng Plateau is a mist-covered volcanic basin, where sulfur pools and gas vents dot the landscape. Scattered ancient temples and ritual legends make it both feared and revered, a sacred highland where ancient good and evil deities once roamed.
districts.name: Dieng Plateau

districts.flavor: Rising above Lake Venado, Mount Apo's name means "revered elder" in Lumad languages. It is a shortened form of Apo Sandawa, the spirit of the sacred mountain, also called "Elder Sandawa" or "Grandfather Sandawa." Rituals for Apo Sandawa are performed by the tribe's shaman who is seen as a medium for ancestor spirits.
districts.name: Mount Apo

districts.flavor: Known as the "Mother Temple of Bali," Besakih is the island's most significant and holiest Hindu temple complex. It is located on the slopes of Mount Agung, Bali's tallest volcano and sacred mountain. It is the island's religious and cultural heart, hosting grand ceremonies for all.
districts.name: Besakih Temple

districts.flavor: Gongsanseong Fortress crowns the hills above the Geum River. Built as Baekje's royal citadel, its long walls and stone gates guarded kings and subjects alike, a mountain stronghold of dynastic power and defense.
districts.name: Gongsanseong Fortress

districts.flavor: Founded by the hermit Li Bo, where white deer roamed freely, the academy flourished as a center of Neo-Confucianism.
districts.name: White Deer Grotto Academy

districts.flavor: This academy drew scholars studying the Classics in Hunan's quiet hills. A hub of poetry and philosophy, it carried Tang traditions into the Song.
districts.name: Shigu Academy

districts.flavor: Scholars built an academy among Mount Culai's peaks to study Confucian texts in seclusion. Its halls echoed with debates on harmonizing nature and governance.
districts.name: Culai Academy

districts.flavor: The Lize Academy promotes scholarship among waters and reeds of Hebei, serving as a northern bastion of Confucian order amid shifting frontiers.
districts.name: Lize Academy

districts.flavor: An academy that trains in ritual, meditation, and sacred texts, serving as a spiritual counterpoint to the Song-era Confucian academies.
districts.name: Maoshan Academy

districts.flavor: Scholarly institution of the Tiantai school, this academy specializes in teaching philosophy and meditation.
districts.name: Tiantai Monasteries

districts.flavor: The Buddhist mountain monastery complex served as a stronghold of Esoteric Buddhism. Pilgrims likened it to India's Vulture Peak.
districts.name: Jizu Shan Temples

districts.flavor: Seat of the Sixth Patriarch Huineng of Chan Buddhism. It remains a vibrant hub for Chan teachings.
districts.name: Nanhua Temple

districts.flavor: The key-hole shaped mounds at Mozu are said to house past emperors of old. For ships in the nearby bay they are a notable landmark as well as a reminder of times past.
districts.name: Mozu Tombs

districts.flavor:
Built upon the site of Saint Peter's tomb at Vatican Hill at the order of Emperor Constantine I after his conversion to Christianity, the Basilica of Saint Peter serves as the center of Christendom in the West. 

This church traditionally serves as the seat of the Roman Catholic Pope and has grown over the centuries into a sprawling complex, protected by the Leonine Wall.
districts.name: Saint Peter's Basilica

districts.flavor:
The Boudha Stupa of Kathmandu, also known as Jarung Kashor and Khāsa Chaitya, is one of the largest stupas in Buddhism, and may be the birthplace of what became the Tibetan branch of Buddhism. Its enormous dome and mandala houses the remains of multiple buddhas and innumerable sacred relics of various shapes and forms. 

Due to its placement on an ancient trade route between Nepal and Tibet, travellers and merchants frequently stop by to rest and pray.
districts.name: Boudhanath

districts.flavor: The mighty Iron Pillar of Delhi stands as a symbol to the glory of King Chandragupta II, though subsequent rulers have also etched their names into it. Despite having stood for a long time, there's no trace of rust – a testament to the skill of Indian ironsmiths!
districts.name: Iron Pillar of Delhi

districts.flavor: The Great Stupa was built by the Mauryan Emperor Ashoka in the third century BC, near the site of his wedding with his wife Devi. The grandiose structure housing relics of the Buddha is one of the oldest of its kind, and it is also famed for its intricately carved torana gateways.
districts.name: Great Stupa of Sanchi

districts.flavor: Built on the site of a fourth century Fire Temple, this illustrious building amazes traveller and pilgrim alike with its great iwans, tiled dome, and its majestic entrance portal with a pair of sky-high minarets.
districts.name: Grand Mosque of Yazd

districts.flavor:
In 708, Saint Aubert, Bishop of Avranches, saw in a dream a vision of the Archangel Michael, instructing him to build an oratory upon a nearby tidal island. Aubert at first ignored this vision, attributing it to a trick by the Devil. Eventually the Archangel managed to convince him - according to legend by poking a hole in his skull with a touch, and the bishop ordered the contruction of a new sanctuary on Mont Tombe. 

Thus begins the history of Mont-Saint-Michel.
districts.name: Mont-Saint-Michel

primaryBuilding.name: Saint Aubert's Oratory to Saint Michael

districts.flavor: This great rectangular tomb of dressed stone is said to belong to an ancient Goguryeo king, though memory of his name has now been lost. The corridors that lead to the tomb are painted with colorful frescoes, and at the top of the pyramid rises a small wooden pavilion honoring the buried.
districts.name: Tomb of a Goguryeo King

districts.flavor: The Daibutsu of Kamakura is a venerable bronze statue of the Amitābha Buddha, weighing several tons and decorated with gilded details. It is enclosed by a great hall inspired by the temples of the southwest and surrounded by thirty-two lotus petals.
districts.name: Great Buddha of Kamakura

districts.flavor: This great stepped pyramid rises from the jungle like a holy mountain, each of its seven terraces holding increasingly ornate shrines and altars. The upper sanctuary crowns the structure, and protects within the sacred lingam of Shiva, the center of a complex axial plan of religious design.
districts.name: Lingapura Pyramid

districts.flavor: The mountain of Maijishan has long been a place of veneration, and along its southern cliffs, considered geomantically auspicious, hundreds of shrines have been carved into the reddish rock, holding statues and colorful frescoes of serene Buddhas and bodhisattvas. Many have been commissioned by the nearby urban families, for which the site is an occasional place of pilgrimage, and meditative contemplation.
districts.name: Maijishan Grottoes
