districts.flavor: From the sprawling temple complex of the city's ruling family stand three tall pagodas of brick walls and stone pedestals. They are the ends of an isosceles triangle, marking the sacred geometry of the site and framing the surrounding mountains and lake.
districts.name: Three Pagodas of Dali

districts.flavor: The monumental lion is the largest cast-iron sculpture in all of China, and on its strong back supports a bodhisattva gently sat upon a lotus pedestal and richly decorated in gilded details. Set near the flood-prone plain, it has become known as a warden against the rising tides to the local citizens.
districts.name: Iron Lion of Cangzhou

districts.flavor: This site has been favored for astronomical observation for centuries, due to its geomantic qualities and symbolic geographic centrality within China. The current structure, a complex trapezoidal shape, serves as a vast sundial, with the tall central ruler casting its shadow into the trench that divides the platform, and marking the passage of the sun.
districts.name: Gaocheng Observatory

districts.flavor: Many structures compose the temple complex, all brick-built and adorned with sandstone detailings. At the center rise the great stupas of Mahligai and Tuo, the former tall and slender, the latter vast like a mountain, towering above the smaller shrines and terraces around them.
districts.name: Candi of Muara Takus

districts.flavor: A nine-story pagoda that stands upon a broad stone pedestal, its pale masonry glowing under the sunlit sky. It is the first of the stone pagodas of Korea, and its form and balanced proportions have made it a model for temple-builders all across the peninsula.
districts.name: Stone Pagoda of Mireuksa

districts.flavor: Over two hundred large kilns cover the site, the largest center of celadon production in the region. The ceramics fired here are known for their coarse, hard-fired texture and distinctive yellow-green glaze, and are traded all across the markets of Southeast Asia.
districts.name: Thuriang Kilns

districts.flavor: One of the most prestigious academies of learning in China, Yuelu has long served as a center for study and examination. Its layout is centered around a main courtyard, from which corollary halls and pavilions, where generations of scholars have prepared for civil service, extend outward in balanced symmetry.
districts.name: Yuelu Academy

districts.flavor: This geological formation is characterized by a great number of rounded, conical hills that stretch uniformly across the landscape. They are cloaked in a layer of grass that - during the dry season - turns a vivid hue of brown and orange, giving the terrain an unusual autumnal flush.
districts.name: Slopes of Russet

districts.flavor: The Fanfang is an important community of foreign merchants - primarily Muslim Arabs and Persians that have come here through the maritime trade routes - which has been granted its own district to the west of the city, with its own officials and customs. At its center stands a red-walled mosque crowned by a tall minaret and lighthouse, guiding ships and souls to the safety of the harbor.
districts.name: Fanfang of Guangzhou

districts.flavor: A sprawling palatial complex of pavilions, halls, temples and courtyards, the Wilwatikta is vast enough to resemble a city of its own. Rectangular brick walls enclose the grounds, and the entrance to the processional avenue is marked by a series of towering Paduraksa gates.
districts.name: Wilwatikta Palace

districts.flavor: This stunning landscape of karst and limestone islets rises from the calm emerald waters of the gulf, where local fishermen drift searching for catch under the shadow of the pillars.
districts.name: Ha Long Bay

districts.flavor: The largest and most refined of the Cham temple complexes, the sanctuary is composed of a series of enclosures scattered close to one another in the forested land, each with its own gates, shrines, and stupas. The structures are all built of red-brick, placed in geometrical patterns, and decorated with sandstone lintels.
districts.name: My Son Sanctuary

districts.flavor: This mountain that raises from the jungle wilderness is sacred to the local people. Amidst the humidity and the mist, its slopes are covered in striking limestone pinnacles and deep caverns carved by the water through countless ages.
districts.name: Gunung Api

districts.flavor: Scattered across the valleys of Central Sulawesi lie many megalithic figures and icons raised by the local people for rituals and to honor the spirits. These effigies, known as arcas, are carved with minimalist precision, their forms traced with subtle and elegant lines.
districts.name: Sulawesi Megaliths

districts.flavor: This great Shinto shrine - a taisha - has been built near the shore, facing the sea. It rises upon a series of enormous wooden pillars and thick trunks, lifting its halls high above the ground where mortals walk, and into the sky where the gods and spirits of the land live.
districts.name: Kizuki Taisha

districts.flavor: The oldest and most influential of all Confucian temples, this vast complex of halls and courtyards has been a model of reference and inspiration for temple builders all across China and beyond, with its harmonious geometrical layout and refined details. Nearby lies a quiet forest where the tombs of Confucius and his descendants have been laid to rest, forming an important place of pilgrimage for devotees.
districts.name: Temple of Confucius

districts.flavor: Built along the northern slopes of the Phoenix Hill, the imperial citadel serves as the seat of the court and its administration, hosting countless scholars and officials in its cavernous halls and corridors. Though not as vast as the palaces of the northern capitals, the refinement and elegance of its terraced gardens and pavilions more than matches them.
districts.name: Imperial Citadel of Lin'an

districts.flavor: In the prosperous city of Indra, the gilded roofs and pinnacles of its temples are countless, each more lavishly decorated than the other with sculpted reliefs and statues of deities and devarajas.
districts.name: Temples of Angkor

districts.flavor: An achievement of engineering worthy of fame, this white marble sentinel stands tall and proud over the city.
districts.name: Tower of Pisa

districts.flavor: This white marble belltower stands tall over the city, although perhaps not quite as tall as it could have been. That it remains standing at all is a testament to the skill of its builders.
districts.name: Leaning Tower of Pisa

districts.flavor: Raised around the hermitage of Saint Gall, this abbey is famed for its school, scriptorium, and library. Within its walls, monks copy sacred texts and train clerics whose learning carries far beyond the shores of Lake Constance.
districts.name: Abbey of St Gall

districts.flavor: Raised above Avignon as both fortress and residence, this palace shelters the papal court behind massive stone walls. Chapels, audience halls, and administrative chambers turn the city into a center of ecclesiastical power.
districts.name: Palais des Papes

districts.flavor: The cathedral church of Rome is mother and head of the churches of the city and the world. In its basilica and adjoining halls councils gather, doctrine is fixed, and the authority of the Roman pontiff is displayed to all.
districts.name: Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran

districts.flavor: At Reims, the cathedral stands as the sacred site of Clovis' baptism and the crowning of kings. Here, the blessing of the clergy can transform a ruler's claims into divine authority, forging a bond between faith and royal power.
districts.name: Reims Cathedral

districts.flavor: An important copper mine, providing incredibly profitable copper ore to whoever is lucky enough to own it.
districts.name: Copper Mines

districts.flavor: A rich silver mine, providing a constant stream of valuable silver.
districts.name: Silver Mines

districts.flavor: An incredibly valuable and rare gold mine, highly sought after by every noble in the region.
districts.name: Gold Mines

districts.flavor: At the foot of Mt. Rammelsberg lies a profitable and ever sought-after silver mine.
districts.name: The Rammelsberg Mines

districts.flavor: The Kutná Hora mine is a large silver mine located on the lands of the Sedlec Monastery. With the support of local Abbots (and German miners) industry in the area is prospering.
districts.name: Kutná Hora Mine

districts.flavor: Silver has been mined in this area for hundreds of years, and with many veins still unexploited this site promises to be a major sources of silver for centuries still.
districts.name: Baofeng Silver Mines

districts.flavor: The Kremnica mountains are abundant in gold. With blood, sweat, and the assistance of a few hundred experienced German miners, that gold will be minted into Florins in no time!
districts.name: Kremnica Mines

districts.flavor: While initially somewhat remote and untamed these mountains harbor immense riches in the form of gold and copper. With proper direction the local small scale mining might be turned into a major source of precious metals.
districts.name: Zijinshan Mines

districts.flavor: Eventually one of the primary mining regions in China the Jiaodong peninsula is the source of vast amounts of gold, waiting to be fully exploited.
districts.name: Jiaodong Mines

districts.flavor: Also known as “Stora Kopparberget” (the Great Copper Mountain) this mine produces vast quantities of copper.
districts.name: The Falun Mines

districts.flavor: The Schwaz silver mine lies at the foot of the Kellerjoch and Eiblschrofen mountains, in the middle of a valley. The opportunity for mining means that a lot of people are drawn to the area.
districts.name: Schwaz Mine

districts.flavor: A major silver mining region for centuries the Lianghze areas mines still have many veins to exploit.
districts.name: The Liangzhe Mines

districts.flavor: The Argentaria del Sigerro is rich in underground silver veins. With sufficient incentive and development, this area could be exploited for vast quantities of precious silver.
districts.name: Argentiera Mine

districts.flavor: The Kollur mines exploit the largest seam of diamonds in all of the Indian subcontinent. The work is extremely dangerous, but the riches are unimaginable.
districts.name: The Kollur Mines

districts.flavor: The Siderokausia mines are rich in silver and gold, and are exploited by twelve separate villages that each run a part of the mines.
districts.name: Siderokausia Mines

districts.flavor: The mines of Mali are truly overflowing with gold. Endless wealth stream from their depths and into the treasuries of the local rulers, who adorn themselves with the precious metal.
districts.name: Gold Mines of Mali

districts.flavor: In Northern Telingana iron is often available in lumps very close to the surface and can be easily mined in large quantities. What is exceptional however is the high quality of the iron, which is unparalleled in the subcontinent and recognized far beyond India's borders.
districts.name: Konasamudram Mines

districts.flavor: The Forest of Dean is the most notable center of iron mining and forging in the British Isles. The many forges here have supplied the region with ironware since long before Roman boots first trod Britain's soil.
districts.name: Mines of the Forest of Dean

districts.flavor: Phnom Dek, or 'Iron Mountain' is one of the more abundant sources of Iron in Southeast Asia, an otherwise rare metal in this part of the world. In the forges here weapons and tools can be made to arm an empire.
districts.name: Mines of Phnom Dek

districts.flavor: This area has been a source of Iron since the days of the Han dynasty and remains an active center of metalworking and mining.
districts.name: Mines of Hanxing

districts.flavor: The Chihu mines have been active since the era of the three kingdoms when the Wu forged weapons here. With rich deposits of Iron and Copper it is a major source of weapon production as well as minting.
districts.name: Chihu Iron Mines

districts.flavor: For thousands of years the Zawar mines have been a rich source of Lead, Zinc, and Silver. The deposits at Zawar are unique not only in their abundance but also in how they are clearly separated in a way that makes it possible to separate the ores from each other manually without more advanced metallurgical processes.
districts.name: The Zawar Mines

districts.flavor: The Air mountains have rich deposits of copper and have been mined in Takkeda since prehistoric times.
districts.name: The Takkeda Mines

districts.flavor: The Khetri hills contain some of the longest mined copper deposits in India and have been a source for copper working for just as long.
districts.name: The Khetri Copper Mines

districts.flavor: The Taghaza Salt Mines is the point of origin for most of the salt of the Maghreb and West Africa.
districts.name: The Taghaza Salt Pan

districts.flavor: Ijil is one of the oldest salt mines in Africa and in many ways one of the first entrepôts of the trans-Saharan trade network.
districts.name: Ijil Salt Mines

districts.flavor: The massive salt massifs of Torda have been central to the economy of Transylvania for centuries. The mines and the salt market remains a great source of income for the region.
districts.name: Torda Salt Mines

districts.flavor: The great deposits of Salt in this area has the potential to keep the entire region supplied. Salt mining will keep the region rich for generations.
districts.name: Wieliczka Salt Mines

districts.flavor: Due to its unique advantages for Salt mining this area has been a point for extracting salt from the depths of the earth since the days of the Shang dynasty, thousands of years ago. Today and for the foreseable future it remains a major factor in the regional economy.
districts.name: Ziliujing & Gongjing Salt Wells

districts.flavor: The Phocaean deposits of Alum are among the most bountiful in the known world. The rare Alum is in high demand by dyers and textile manufacturers all over the European continent.
districts.name: The Phocaea Alum Mines

districts.flavor: The Pansjhir valley has been a known source of silver and emeralds since the days of Alexander the Great. Hindu, Buddhists and eventually Muslim dynasties have mined silver and minted their coins in this area.
districts.name: The Pansjhir Mines

districts.flavor: Situated on the slopes of Kopaonik, Trepča is an area that has been mined for silver since Roman times. While it was closed down in the early middle ages it still holds very rich deposits of precious metals.
districts.name: The Trepča Mines

districts.flavor: Rudnik, the mountain of Mines, is rich in silver, lead and copper and has seen continuous mining for hundreds of years.
districts.name: The Rudnik Mines

districts.flavor: The deep mines of the Cévennes mountains have been built to extract the copper based silver deposits of the region.
districts.name: The Cévennes Mines

districts.flavor: Guiyang has been the site of Imperial mints for over a thousand years. Dynasty after dynasty has safeguarded the local silver mines and issued currency with their product as their standard.
districts.name: The Guiyang Mines

districts.flavor: In a region that has an unquenchably thirst for coinage there is always a need for silver mines. This area has served the Imperial mints with raw material for generations.
districts.name: The Kaibao Mines

districts.flavor: Khotan has been the source of Hetian jade since the beginning of time. This precious white stone is the most highly prized of all jade, valued higher than either gold or silver by many. Jade is mined both directly out of the mountain and picked directly from open pits and riverbeds.
districts.name: The Khotan Mines

districts.flavor: One of the four great jades of China, Dushan has been a jade mining location since the Han dynasty. Different from other types of jade both in that it has a richer color, which is also often more mixed than for other types.
districts.name: The Dushan Mines

districts.flavor: This ancient quarry has supplied its community with high-quality jade for several millennia. The Hongshan people discovered and enjoyed all sorts of craftsmanship, such as bracelets, tools, and symbolic artifacts, from it, enriching social uses and familial reputation.
districts.name: Xiuyan Jade Mines

districts.flavor: The Kotakigawa River runs through the gorge at the base of Mt. Myojo and is rich in large jade deposits. These deposits produce some of the most exquisite jade in the region and beyond, delighting the eye with their vibrant green color.
districts.name: Itoigawa Jade Mines

districts.flavor: The hills of Lantian have been a source of high-quality jade for thousands of years. This pale stone, historically carved into imperial seals and celebrated by Tang poets, is valued not for its abundance but for its distinctive beauty and status.
districts.name: Lantian Jade Mines

districts.flavor: Nestled along the island's central heights, Fengtian Jade Mines facilitate maritime trade in precious stones. Favored by authorities, locals, and traders from distant lands, this luminous green jade holds a special place in the county's revenue.
districts.name: Fengtian Jade Mines

districts.flavor: Deep beneath forested hills, veins of bright jadeite shimmer amid tangled rivers and limestone ridges. For many years, these deposits were hidden from passersby and foreign traders, offering locals numerous boulders of the valuable green stone.
districts.name: Hpakant Jade Mines

districts.flavor: Known to chroniclers simply as the mining country, the mountains of the Eastern Egyptian desert harbor deep gold deposits. The main hub of this region is Wadi al-Allaq and its mines.
districts.name: The Wadi al-Allaq Mines

districts.flavor: Transylvania has been mined for gold since before Roman times and remains ripe for contemporary re-exploitation.
districts.name: The Verespatak Mines

districts.flavor: Also called the Island of Gold, the caverns of the Barisan Mountains contain numerous veins of the valuable mineral. Small mining outposts are spread across its foothills, digging deep and wide for the precious gold.
districts.name: The Suvarnadvipa Mines

districts.flavor: Turquoise is a stone that can be found in many places but nowhere is it as abundant and as high quality as in the mountains near Nishapur. The stones are also very easily accessible even without very deep pits.
districts.name: The Nishapur Mines

districts.flavor: Mined in antiquity for its enormous silver deposits Srebrenica, Silver City, is ripe to be exploited again using modern mining techniques.
districts.name: Srebrenica Mine

districts.flavor: Ratnapura, the city of Gems, is one of the world's most significant sources of rubies, and sapphires. For hundreds of years these riches have been mined and traded with merchants from the Indian subcontinent, South East Asia and China.
districts.name: The Ratnapura Mines

districts.flavor: The main source of lapis lazuli in the world, the mines of Sar-i Sang have been active since prehistoric times, and their blue stones could be seen in all the courts of antiquity. Local workers toil here night and day to extract the vaunted blue stones.
districts.name: The Sar-i Sang Mines

districts.flavor:
Mogok Valley is famous for its rubies and sapphires, as well as less valuable stones such as spinel or garnet.
What makes 'the valley of rubies' stand out even more than quantity is the quality of the stones. As the deep red stones are excavated from the earth they sparkle in the basting sun in a way that has no equal anywhere else.
districts.name: The Mogok Valley Mines

districts.flavor: The island of Kinka and its associated Koganeyama Shrine are famous for the earliest discovered gold deposits in Japan, in the form of gold dust. Established by Emperor Shōmu in the 8th century, the shrine is dedicated to Kanayama, god of mining.
districts.name: Kinka Gold Mine

districts.flavor: The island of Tsushima is famed for its silver deposits, discovered in the late 7th century during the reign of Emperor Tenmu. Rich in galena, the black ores of the Sea of Japan yield many riches.
districts.name: Tsushima Silver Mine

districts.flavor: An old place of exile, few would have expected the distant island of Sado could secretly be hoarding such a wealth of gold beneath its surface.
districts.name: Sado Gold Mine

districts.flavor: Beneath the village of Tada, nestled in the Hokusetsu mountains, a wealth of precious metals lies waiting to be rendered. It is said the plating of the great Buddha of Tōdai-ji was hewn from this place.
districts.name: Tada Copper Mine

districts.flavor: A large trading compound, serving as a place for republics and wealthy patricians to trade their goods and services.

tierConcept:
All built Districts have a tier, starting at I, which signifies the level of the main District Building.

Upgrading the tier of a District is also the main way to unlock more building slots in the District, as well as more options for Buildings in a District.
Standard Districts and Duchy Capital Districts have 4 levels (I to IV), with every level unlocking a new building slot and additional choices.
Resource Districts have 10 tiers, with III, V and VII unlocking additional building slots.
Great Project or Special Districts often have only 1 level and no building slots.

types.desc:
A Holding District is the core District of a Holding, representing the settlement itself.

Its primary Building is the Holding's main structure, such as a Castle Holding, City Holding, or Temple Holding, which determines the Holding's type. Upgrading that Building raises the Holding's tier, and the District houses further Buildings tied to that type. That main Building also carries the Holding's food Need, so its call on Food Supply grows as the settlement does.

Every Holding has exactly one Holding District, and it cannot be replaced with a District of another type.
types.name: Holding District

types.desc:
Standard Districts are the basic Districts that can be constructed in any Holding.

As Settlement Size increases, the Holding gets more slots for Standard Districts.

If a Holding loses a slot, one District becomes inactive and gives no benefits until a slot is regained. Which District that stays active, and also gets its Building Needs filled first, can be prioritized by dragging and dropping the Districts.
types.name: Standard District

types.desc:
A Resource District extracts the raw Trade Goods a County is suited to produce, such as Wood, Iron, Grain, or Cattle. The Buildings available depend on the County's Potential Production.

All of their Production flows into the local Trade Market, shared out among its Buildings in Market Priority order to meet their Needs; the rest becomes a Surplus sold through Trade.

Replacing a Resource District changes which Trade Good the Holding focuses on, but tears down its extraction Building and everything tied to the old Good with no refund.
types.name: Resource District

types.desc:
Duchy Districts are powerful Districts that can only be constructed in the De Jure Capital of a Duchy. Only one type can be constructed in each Duchy.

Duchy Districts are only active if the owner also holds the associated Duchy Title.

Many Buildings in Duchy Districts have modifiers that affect all Holdings in the Duchy, making them powerful tools for specializing your Domain.
types.name: Duchy District

types.desc:
Special Districts are unique Districts that are present in a few predetermined places around the world.

Examples include ancient wonders, grand cathedrals, and notable mines. Some are already constructed at the start of the game, while others have to be constructed.

Special Districts are usually very powerful, and well worth fighting for.
types.name: Special District

types.desc:
Great Districts are unique Districts, and are constructed as a result of Great Projects. One famous example is the Great Walls of China.

Great Districts are usually very powerful, but their utility is tied to specific conditions.
types.name: Great District

types.desc:
Trade Posts are a type of District that only a Patrician of a Republic can construct.

Unlike other Districts, a Trade Post can be built in a distant County the Patrician does not own, extending their commercial reach far beyond their Domain. It can serve as the starting point for Trade Routes, while its Buildings provide powerful Trade bonuses. Some also grant unique privileges, such as recruiting troops or Mercenaries abroad.

The number of Trade Posts a character may hold is capped by their Trade Post Limit. Exceeding this limit incurs penalties.
types.name: Trade Post District

types.desc:
Entrepôt Districts are unique trading Districts that facilitate trade over long distances.

Instead of producing Trade Goods itself, an Entrepôt District has Needs that can only be met by the imports of Profit Routes. These Goods are then resold in the local Market.

This way, an Entrepôt District acts as a distribution spot for Trade Goods, allowing for Trade Goods to be moved multiple times by different Trade Routes.

Entrepôt Districts cannot be constructed and are located in historically predetermined places around the world.
types.name: Entrepôt District
